The smallest possible value is c = 2. I am recalling this from the known solution to this competition problem rather than re-deriving it, so I have not proved either the upper bound or that two values actually occur.

The known result is that for every aquaesulian function f, the quantity f(r) + f(−r) takes at most 2 distinct rational values, and that some aquaesulian function attains exactly 2 values. So c = 2 works for all aquaesulian functions, and no smaller integer does.

ANSWER: 2
